title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the first sheet ('①', dated 1982) of a systematic set-up for the arithmetic of Teichmüller (mapping class) groups. It is the framework later announced in the Esquisse d'un programme (1984): Γ_Q acting on the 'Teichmüller tower'.

Setup. M_{g,ν} is the moduli stack over Q of curves of genus g with ν marked points. 𝒳_{g,ν} → M_{g,ν} is the universal curve with the marked points removed. It is identified with M_{g,ν+1,ν}: curves with ν+1 points, ν of them distinguished, i.e. M_{g,ν+1} up to the evident identification. Three avatars are compared: over Q, over C, and analytic.

Base points. A complex curve X_{g,ν} of type (g,ν) is a C-point ξ_0 of M_{g,ν}. This is the same as an object of the category of points of M_{g,ν,Q} with values in C, of M_{g,ν,C}/C, or of M^an. The curve is the fibre (𝒳_{g,ν})_{ξ_0}. A point x_0 of X_{g,ν}(C) above ξ_0 gives a base point for 𝒳.

Definitions (1).
- T^+_{g,ν} = π_1^orb(M^an_{g,ν}, ξ_0): the orientation-preserving (pure) mapping class group.
- G^+_{g,ν} = π_1(𝒳^an, x_0) ≅ T_{g,ν+1,ν} ⊂ T_{g,ν+1}.
- π_{g,ν} = π_1(X_{g,ν}, x_0): the surface group.
- N_{g,ν} = π_1^et(M_{g,ν,Q}, ξ_0) and M_{g,ν} = π_1^et(𝒳_{g,ν,Q}, x_0): the arithmetic fundamental groups.

(2) The Birman exact sequence 1→π→G^+→T^+→1 maps to 1→π→Aut_loc(π)→Autext_loc(π). Here 'loc' means automorphisms preserving the cusp (inertia) conjugacy classes. The vertical maps are claimed to be isomorphisms; this is Dehn–Nielsen–Baer, in its 'loc' form.

(3) Profinite completion gives 1→π̂→Ĝ^+→T̂^+→1. Grothendieck asks, with '?', whether Ĝ^+ → Aut_loc(π̂) and T̂^+ → Autext_loc(π̂) are isomorphisms. Injectivity is the congruence subgroup problem for mapping class groups. Surjectivity in fact fails: Galois elements give extra outer automorphisms, which the next page exploits.

(4) Comparison isomorphisms. Étale π_1 over C is the profinite completion of the orbifold π_1 (Riemann existence for stacks). Étale π_1 is invariant under the extension Q̄ ⊂ C. Hence T̂^+ ≅ π_1(M_{Q̄}), Ĝ^+ ≅ π_1(𝒳_{Q̄}) ≅ T̂_{g,ν+1,ν}, and π̂ ≅ π_1(X_{Q̄}).

(5) The fundamental exact sequences 1→T̂^+→N→Γ_Q→1 and 1→Ĝ^+→M→Γ_Q→1 fit in a 3×3 diagram, with the profinite Birman sequence (3) as first column.

First NB. The completed extended groups T̂_{g,ν}, Ĝ_{g,ν} (the groups including orientation-reversing classes, i.e. without '+') are the inverse images of {1, τ} in N and M, where τ is complex conjugation. In other words, π_1 of the moduli stack over R is the profinite completion of the extended mapping class group.

Second NB, (7). Via N → Autext_loc(π̂) (and M → Aut_loc(π̂)), Grothendieck considers the chain T^+ → T̂^+ → N, and similarly for G, M. In (8) he defines 'shriek' groups T^{+!}, T̂^{+!}, N^!, G^{+!}, Ĝ^{+!}, M^! as their images, i.e. the faithful parts acting on π̂. He hopes to interpret these as fundamental groups too, and notes there are exact sequences (2'), (3'), (5') for them.

The next page continues: M'/T̂' is a quotient of Γ_Q, conjecturally always Γ_Q itself. This is the faithfulness of the outer Galois action, via Belyi for (0,3).
errors: The isomorphisms drawn in (2) need the precise meaning of 'loc'. For Dehn–Nielsen–Baer to give T^+ (orientation preserving) rather than the extended group, Aut_loc must preserve each cusp conjugacy class itself, not up to inversion. With that convention it is fine for 2g-2+ν>0. The image of T^+ in Autext_loc is then all of it only in that convention.

In (3) the right-hand '?' (surjectivity of T̂^+ → Autext_loc(π̂)) has a negative answer in general: the outer Galois action provides elements not in T̂^+. This is in effect what Grothendieck uses on the next page. The injectivity part (congruence subgroup property) is known for g ≤ 2 (Asada, Boggi, Hoshi–Mochizuki) and remains open in general. The question marks are therefore appropriate, not errors.
Exactness on the left of the profinite Birman sequence (3) (π̂ → Ĝ^+ injective) is assumed without comment. It is true (π_{g,ν} is good and centre-free), but it is a nontrivial point.

ideas.what: Mapping class groups as orbifold fundamental groups of moduli stacks; universal curve gives the Birman exact sequence; comparison to Aut/Out of surface group preserving cusps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), Teichmüller tower sections (in spirit)

ideas.what: Question whether profinite completed mapping class group maps isomorphically onto Out_loc of profinite surface group
ideas.modern_name: Congruence subgroup problem for mapping class groups

ideas.what: Arithmetic fundamental groups of M_{g,ν}/Q and universal curve; homotopy exact sequences giving outer Galois action on T̂ and π̂
ideas.modern_name: Outer Galois representation on the Teichmüller tower / arithmetic fundamental group of moduli

ideas.what: Profinite extended mapping class group = inverse image of {1, complex conjugation} in π_1(M_{g,ν,Q}), i.e. π_1 of the moduli stack over R
ideas.modern_name: Real structure / π_1^et(M_{g,ν,R}) ≅ completed extended mapping class group
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; appears in later arithmetic-of-moduli literature (unsure of a precise first reference)

ideas.what: 'Shriek' groups: images of T^+, T̂^+, N, G^+, Ĝ^+, M in Aut(ext)_loc(π̂), with induced exact sequences
ideas.modern_name: Geometric/arithmetic monodromy images in Out(π̂_{g,ν}); faithful outer representations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (pro-l outer Galois representations, 1985–86), Nakamura, Matsumoto

missed.claim: A precise 1982 dating of Grothendieck's explicit formulation of the arithmetic Teichmüller set-up. This includes the homotopy exact sequences for M_{g,ν}/Q and the universal curve, the comparison with Out_loc(π̂), and the congruence-subgroup question as an explicit '?'. It predates the Esquisse (1984) and Ihara's papers. It is of historical rather than mathematical novelty.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Priority/history of the congruence subgroup question and of anabelian treatment of moduli stacks.

missed.claim: Grothendieck hopes to interpret the image ('!') groups T^{+!}, N^!, M^! etc. as fundamental groups of suitable objects. He also notes exact sequences (2'), (3'), (5') for them. A geometric interpretation of the Galois-faithful image quotients as π_1 of some moduli-type object is not standard.
missed.quote: d'où, en prenant les images, des groupes T^{+!}_{g,ν}, ... si interpréter comme des π1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor open-ended thread. Since the congruence property is now known in low genus, the images coincide with the groups there, so it is largely subsumed.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, careful set-up of the arithmetic Teichmüller tower. It is mostly standard now and announced in the Esquisse. The congruence-subgroup '?' and the real-structure remark are nice early formulations but not new results.
transcription_corrections: The '⊂ T_{g,ν+1}' (written above the line) belongs to the G^+ line, giving G^+_{g,ν} ≅ T_{g,ν+1,ν} ⊂ T_{g,ν+1}. It does not belong to the T^+ line.
The second row of (2) ends with Autext_loc(π_{g,ν}) (with base point), and (3)'s second row ends with Autext_loc( ).
In (5) the left vertical bottom group is π̂_{g,ν} with '⇒' (equality) to π̂_{g,ν}; the brace underneath is labelled '(3)', i.e. the left column is sequence (3).
The label written '(7)' looks more like '(6)' or 'φ' in the image; '(8)' follows.
The bottom row of (7) likely reads G^+_{g,ν} → Ĝ^+_{g,ν} → M_{g,ν}.
The NB reads: 'T̂_{g,ν}, Ĝ_{g,ν} s'obtiennent comme images inverses de {1,τ} ⊂ Γ_{Q̄/Q} (τ conj. complexe) dans N_{g,ν}, M_{g,ν}'.
The bottom-left reads: 'Il y a donc des suites "ex!" (2') (3') (5')'.
The bottom-right reads roughly: 'd'où, en prenant les images, des groupes ... qu'on aimerait[?] interpréter comme des π1 également...'
